text:
deploy-bot: Deploy started: rollout v2.14 -> eu-central canary 10% at 11:07 UTC
incident-bot: Automatic canary check: elevated 5xx rate detected on eu-central canary group (threshold 1.5% -> 8.9%). Paging on-call. :rotating_light:
Sam: oncall here, pulling logs now. 
Jessica: I see a spike of 503s from the model-proxy layer, same time as canary ramp.
Kai: adding more context — traffic was routed with new routing-policy v3 (sticky->stateless) in canary. Could be session affinity break.
Sam: good call. Running: `kubectl logs -l app=model-proxy -n eu --since=5m | grep 503 | head`
Sam: output shows repeated `upstream read: connection reset by peer` to model-backend-quant nodes.
Jessica: backend nodes are also reporting increased connection drops in kernel logs. Might be new kernel param from node image bump in this deploy.
Megan: tagging infra and runtime. @eng-runtime can we pause rollouts?
deploy-bot: Rollout paused by sam at 11:12 UTC. Traffic hold applied — new canary traffic halted.
Sam: doing quick canary rollback to previous revision `v2.13` for model-proxy. `kubectl set image` rolling restart.
Kai: I also flipped the routing-policy feature flag `ff-routing-v3` to off for eu region (kill-switch). `curl -X POST https://ff.redwood/api/toggle -d '{"ff-routing-v3": false, "region":"eu-central"}'`
incident-bot: Feature flag flip detected: ff-routing-v3=false (actor: kai).
Sam: rolling back proxy pods now. Observing decreasing 503s in metrics (Grafana panel).
Customer-alert-bot: 11:16 UTC — customer-facing error rate in EU up 2.2% (5xx). Impact: interactive customers may see transient failures and retries.
Jessica: confirm after rollback: metrics show 5xx returning to baseline ~0.3% in 3 minutes. Latency also normalizing.
Megan: good. Are there any lingering degraded backend nodes? Kai, please run health-check across model-backend-quant nodes and post results.
Kai: `for pod in $(kubectl get pods -l role=quant -n eu -o name); do kubectl exec $pod -- curl -sS localhost:8080/health || echo $pod failed; done`
Kai: all backend pods healthy now. No kernel oom or cgroup kills reported in last 15m.
Sam: initiating formal rollback history entry and incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-31245
Sam: current action items: 1) run binary diff on node images used in canary vs baseline, 2) validate routing-policy unit tests and canary gating logic, 3) run soak in staging with routing-policy toggled.
Megan: handoff to evening oncall at 18:00 UTC. @jessica you'll take post-mortem owner. If anything reappears, escalate to infra.
Jessica: acknowledged. I'll collect logs, smoke test customers, and prepare a blameless post-mortem.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity downgraded to SEV2 at 11:24 UTC.
Sam: adding note to ticket: customers affected largely EU interactive flows, roughly 0.8% of requests retried client-side. No data loss.
Customer-alert-bot: Sent status update to affected customers at 11:30 UTC — "We observed a brief increase in errors during a canary deploy; we've rolled back the canary and applied a routing policy kill-switch. We're monitoring."
Jessica: uploading logs and timeline to the ticket, will include a recommended preflight checklist for routing-policy changes.
Sam: thanks team. Follow-up: schedule a joint runtime+infra debug session tomorrow 09:00 UTC to root cause kernel/conn reset interplay.
Megan: noted. Closing thread for now — keep monitoring dashboards for 2 hours. :white_check_mark:
